title: Death and the Maiden
why: The pale maiden arches away in a S-curve with drapery in both hands while Death grips her from behind, a white figure on near-black reading as one backward-leaning shape.

title: Lich's Mastery (Magic: The Gathering, Dominaria)
why: A figure arches back with head thrown and mouth open, one hand clutching a violet glow at the chest, among red candles and pale drapes.

title: Untitled (1973)
why: A thin figure drapes over a black monolith with one arm flung up toward a glowing orange head and the other hanging with red hands, on a rust-orange cloud field.

title: Laocoon and His Sons
artist: Hagesandros, Athenodoros and Polydoros of Rhodes (Vatican copy)
why: The central figure throws his head back with one arm bent behind, a fist clamped on a serpent that winds around his body, a marble study of the struck body entangled in snakes.

title: Ecstasy of Saint Teresa
license: CC BY-SA 4.0 (photo: Livioandronico2013); sculpture public domain
why: A pale figure swoons back under a fan of gilded rods that read as one shaft of golden light falling from above onto a white body.

title: The Nightmare
license: public domain painting (photo on Commons: CC BY 2.5, Tulip Hysteria)
why: A white-robed figure hangs backward off a bed with head thrown down and one arm trailing to the floor, a pale diagonal in a deep red-and-black room.

title: Kaen (jacket of the 2019 Full Edition EP)
artist: Queen Bee (jacket artwork credit not checked)
why: The source pose: a figure leans far back with a head of blue flame, one hand flung out to the left and the other hanging low, on a flat orange-red field.

title: Kel'Thuzad (Heroes of the Storm key art)
why: A skeletal lich in blue-and-gold robes with ruby gems stands with one clawed hand raised and the other low trailing a blue wisp, a symmetrical bone-and-gem silhouette.

title: Death on the Pale Horse
why: A cloaked skull-faced rider floats high on a pale horse through a black sky of flying monsters, with a long scythe diagonal.

title: Vecna (Dungeons & Dragons)
artist: Credited nord-sol.com on the image (Wizards of the Coast; unverified)
why: A horned, gaunt lich with a glowing eye and long claws floats in a dark pillared hall with a spellbook hovering at his hand and one cold shaft of light behind.

title: Transi of Rene de Chalon
why: A standing decayed figure lifts its heart toward the sky with one arm stretched high, a pale vertical column against a dark painted panel, an offering held up.

title: The Ancient of Days (Europe a Prophecy, frontispiece)
why: A bent figure inside a golden sun disc reaches down through black clouds with compasses, a ring of amber light with a V of rays beneath.

title: Skeleton contemplating a skull, lateral view (De humani corporis fabrica, 1543; 1940 photolithograph)
license: CC BY 4.0 (Wellcome Collection photolithograph of a public-domain 1543 woodcut)
why: A lone skeleton leans on a tomb with its chin in one hand and the other hand resting on a skull, one pondering diagonal from skull to heel.

title: Tabulae sceleti et musculorum, Tab. VIII: skeleton from behind with the rhinoceros Clara
artist: Bernhard Siegfried Albinus (engraved by Charles Grignion after Jan Wandelaar)
why: A skeleton seen from behind with one arm flung wide and the other loose, spine and ribs as a clear S, standing before a huge dark animal.

title: Tabulae sceleti et musculorum, Tab. IV: skeleton from the front with the rhinoceros
artist: Bernhard Siegfried Albinus (engraved by Charles Grignion after Jan Wandelaar)
why: A front-view skeleton in a loose contrapposto, one arm thrown out with the hand trailing and the other hanging, legs together with a pointed foot, a calm lich-like stance.

title: Memento Mori: a skeleton in a niche
why: A skeleton sprawls in a niche with one hand lifted and a long banner whipping above, the whole body one S-curve of bone and cloth.

title: The Penitent Magdalene (Magdalen with the Night Light)
why: A single flame in a glass lights a woman's face and a skull in her lap in near-black, one amber light source on dark.

title: Still Life with a Skull (Vanitas)
why: A skull sits between a clear glass flask with a tulip and an hourglass on a pale ledge against black, glass and bone as quiet objects.

title: Osteographia, plate XXXVI: skeleton kneeling
why: A skeleton kneels in profile with palms pressed together and the skull tilted up, one long diagonal from knee to raised head.

title: Skeleton leaning on a spade (De humani corporis fabrica)
license: CC BY 4.0 (Wellcome Collection image of a public-domain 1543 woodcut)
why: A frontal skeleton rests one elbow on a spade handle with the other arm hanging loose, relaxed and facing the viewer, mountains behind.

title: Danse Macabre (Tallinn fragment)
why: A long horizontal frieze of ghoulish Deaths each dancing beside a robed figure under banners, a ready composition for a wide banner format.

title: Eve, the Serpent, and Death
why: A decayed Death stands beside Eve while a thick serpent loops a tree trunk, pale bodies and a metal-grey snake ring against black.

title: The Triumph of Death
why: A burnt amber and ember-orange plain under a black-red sky is crowded with bone-white skeletons, showing how a warm horizon holds hundreds of pale figures.

title: In ictu oculi
why: A gold-brown skeleton strides out of a black arch, one hand snuffing a candle and the other holding a coffin and scythe, with a tiara, crown and globe in gold and red below.

title: Skeletons Fighting over a Hanged Man
why: Two skeletons in hats, shawls and a red skirt tug a hanged figure in a pale room ringed by masks, bones dressed in cloth with a mask-like skull.

title: Dance of Death: The Trumpeters of Death
why: Skeletons blow trumpets and hit kettledrums under a stone arch, bold black hatching and white bones forming strong diagonals.

title: Takiyasha the Witch and the Skeleton Spectre (triptych)
why: A giant cream-white skeleton fills two panels, skull and ribcage towering over tiny figures, the scale a poster-ready bone silhouette on grey.

title: Beauty surrounded by skeletons (hanging scroll)
why: Pale ink skeletons gather round a woman and one in a top hat pulls her sleeve, bones drawn light and playful on cream silk.

title: The Ghost of Kohada Koheiji (One Hundred Ghost Stories)
why: A skull with exposed bone peers sideways out of a red mosquito net, one clawed hand hooked over the edge, as a flat red-on-blue colour block.

title: Oya Taro Mitsukuni Watching Skeletons (Wakan hyaku monogatari)
why: A host of grey ghost-skeletons with swords, bows and a lantern swarm in pure black space around a seated samurai, pale bones on black with one red scabbard.

title: Holy Body of Saint Gratian (Waldsassen Basilica)
artist: Unknown (17th-18th century catacomb saint), photo by Wolfgang Sauber
why: A whole skeleton stands dressed in a gem-studded, gold-embroidered court dress under glass with a gilt arch around it, a bone figure fully set with jewels.

title: Hand of Sabazios (votive hand)
why: A verdigris bronze hand raised in blessing, two fingers up and a serpent coiling on the thumb side, with small figures and a shrine below: the actual Sabazios object.

title: Relics of Saint Munditia (Peterskirche, Munich)
why: A crowned skeleton lies in a black and silver glass reliquary in red gem-set brocade, candles at each end and a smaller skull above, bones laid out like a sleeping figure.

title: Skeleton of Saint Innocentius (Basilica of St. Lorenz, Kempten)
why: A skull with gold-filigree plates set with gems over the eye sockets, a gold-leaf laurel and pearl strands, hands layered with rubies and ruby-red velvet.

title: Phylactery Lich (Magic: The Gathering, Magic 2011)
why: A hooded skeletal lich with glowing violet eyes holds a staff hung with a glowing orb inside a cave of stalagmites, a cave-and-light setup close to the game.

title: Demilich (Magic: The Gathering, Adventures in the Forgotten Realms)
why: A skull in a stone niche with cut-diamond eyes and gem shards for teeth, bone and glittering facets in one object.

title: Acererak the Archlich (Magic: The Gathering, Adventures in the Forgotten Realms)
why: A crowned, masked skeletal lich lunges with a hooked staff carrying a floating ghost skull, in a teal stone crypt with swirls of pale smoke.

title: Death (Castlevania: Symphony of the Night)
artist: Ayami Kojima (credit as listed on the Castlevania wiki file; unverified)
why: A skull under a deep blue hood and checkered collar grips a scythe whose long blade and pole make two clean diagonals on a white ground.

title: Untitled (1984)
why: Two emaciated skeletal figures embrace on a flat amber-orange field, bone-brown bodies with no background, a warm reverent tone.

title: Lich (Dungeons & Dragons 5e Monster Manual)
artist: Wizards of the Coast (artist not verified)
why: A robed lich throws one arm out with a long clawed hand while the other hangs in shredded sleeves, a clean flung-claw silhouette on plain white.

title: Lich (Dungeons & Dragons 2025 Monster Manual)
artist: Vik Menezes (credit printed on the image)
why: A lich with head back and open mouth raises one clawed hand in a swirl of teal glyph light over floating tomes, in a ruin lit amber from behind.

title: Gravelord Nito (Dark Souls)
why: A giant assembled from stacked small skeletons holds one amber flame in a near-black frame, the flame the only warm light.

title: Skull Knight (Berserk, manga panel)
why: A bone-white skeletal knight on a skeletal horse in cloak and rib-plate with a rose mark, hard black-and-white inking in a forest.
